correctness.rationale: The full proof counts exactly floor(u_i-delta) priority-stack entries at least delta+1 and shows they are necessarily removed before any lower entry. This reconstructs the tie-independent exact entry time and state for arbitrary real starting data. From a strictly subunit head spread, chosen heads drop beneath all unchosen heads, forcing one of each index in m steps. Equal-share drift cancels after each block; coordinate integrality forces any period to be divisible by m. Explicit edge cases m=2, ties, negative and nonzero-sum initial vectors, and unbounded tau are covered. 3403 independent exact-rational regression tests passed; finite tests do not serve as universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full recent preprint distinguishes initial-cube Q-periodicity (Theorem 6.1) from global eventual period divisible by Q (Theorem 6.4) and explicitly leaves global exact Q unresolved (Problem 6.3). Equal shares give Q=m: the present all-real exact entry time and entry vector plus least period m are not implications of either stated theorem. A same-source previous finding concerns irrational three-party mean-square discrepancy. Older convex dynamics sources give boundedness and limited-dimensional fundamental-domain entry without an inspected all-dimensional floor-sum formula. This is a best-evidence comparison, with residual historical risk from an abstract-only 2009 source and implicit scheduling literature.

value.rationale: The uniform-share family is the canonical symmetric rational subfamily of a clearly stated global eventual-period problem. All-real initial conditions, all candidate numbers, exact first entrance time, tie-independent entry vector, and fully determined infinite tail identify natural dynamical invariants not obtainable from abstract eventual periodicity or compact boundedness. The exact transient is unbounded even at fixed m. The result resolves the equal-share case without pretending to settle unequal shares.
